channel.title: AI Daily Watch: AI news, innovation & trends
channel.description: Major model releases, agents, enterprise adoption, funding and deals, regulation in the UK, EU and US, research and open models.

item.title: Cohere completes acquisitions of AISLE and cubic
item.description: Cohere: Cohere announced it has completed its acquisition of AISLE, which builds systems for vulnerability discovery and remediation, and welcomed the team behind AI code-review platform cubic. The deals add cybersecurity and secure software-development capabilities to Cohere’s enterprise and sovereign-AI offerings.

item.title: MIT reports AI copilot using human feedback to improve structural designs
item.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology: MIT researchers reported an AI-assisted design system that identifies likely areas for human revision in algorithmically generated structures. In the paper summarized by MIT, the approach produced designs that were easier to manufacture and had higher buckling loads, with about 15 seconds added to design time compared with fully algorithmic approaches.

item.title: Thinking Machines makes Inkling 2 Small weights downloadable
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab: Thinking Machines Lab updated its Inkling 2 Small release announcement to say the model weights are available for download on Hugging Face. The change expands access for developers and researchers who want to run or adapt the model beyond hosted API use.

item.title: Conductor reverses course and resumes development
item.description: Conductor: Conductor founder Charlie Holtz said the team had decided to continue developing the AI coding-agent product and that regular updates would resume the following week, reversing the earlier plan to wind it down. The post does not specify whether the previously announced Conductor Cloud shutdown schedule also changed.

item.title: Anthropic opens self-hosted Claude Managed Agents to private beta
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic introduced a private beta that lets organizations run Claude Managed Agents in their own cloud or on-premises environment, hosting agents, credentials, and session history themselves. This gives enterprises more control over their agent infrastructure and data location, while the announcement describes a beta rather than general availability.

item.title: Sompo Holdings and NTT partner to explore physical AI in nursing care
item.description: Sompo Holdings and NTT: Sompo Holdings and NTT agreed to study real-world physical-AI deployment in Japan’s nursing-care sector, with labor shortages as a key motivation. Initial potential use cases include support tasks such as cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and moving items, while the companies assess pathways from demonstrations to commercialization.

item.title: MIT researchers develop a more data-efficient method for climate AI models
item.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology: MIT researchers reported a method for training climate-emulation AI with a smaller, carefully optimized synthetic dataset. Their report says the resulting models were more adaptable to scenarios not seen in training, potentially making useful climate tools faster to produce and update.

item.title: European Commission issues guidance on AI Act transparency obligations
item.description: European Commission: The European Commission published guidance on implementing the AI Act’s Article 50 transparency obligations for certain AI systems. The guidance provides an implementation reference for organizations subject to the Act’s AI transparency requirements.

item.title: Kindo raises $30 million to expand enterprise AI-agent controls
item.description: Kindo: Kindo announced a $30 million financing expansion, bringing its total capital raised to $57.6 million. It plans to expand go-to-market operations and develop its platform for discovering, monitoring, and governing enterprise AI-agent activity.

item.title: Google DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2 for cell-specific DNA predictions
item.description: Google DeepMind: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a model designed to predict how genetic variants affect specific human cell types and states. The company reports nearly twice as many identified causal variants on a benchmark compared with its prior state of the art; the model is available for non-commercial research and in a commercial-research preview.

item.title: Databricks plans roughly $3 billion investment across Europe and the Middle East
item.description: Databricks: Databricks announced plans to invest about $3 billion across Europe and the Middle East, expanding regional teams and supporting adoption of its AI and agent products. The investment could deepen its enterprise presence and capacity to help regional customers build and scale AI systems.

item.title: Salesforce releases autonomous R&D agents that improve AI models
item.description: Salesforce: Salesforce introduced SFR-AutoR&D, a system of agents designed to carry out research loops, improve codebases, and train models. Salesforce reports that its use on EmbeddingGemma 2 produced a new embedding model with better quality and latency, illustrating a potential route to automated enterprise model improvement.

item.title: Alibaba opens Qwen4-Max multimodal model in preview
item.description: Alibaba: Alibaba made Qwen4-Max-Preview, its next-generation flagship multimodal model, available for a limited preview. The model is described as supporting text, image and video understanding, deep reasoning, and agentic tasks; preview access is through Token Plan.

item.title: Rox raises $100 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation
item.description: Rox: AI sales startup Rox announced a $100 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation. Reuters reported that the company plans to use the funding to advance AI research, develop custom models, and expand its enterprise customer base.

item.title: Plurai raises $13 million to build a simulation layer for AI agents
item.description: Plurai: Plurai raised a $13 million seed round led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity, and Mercer. The startup is developing a simulation layer to test AI agents in unpredictable environments, aiming to address reliability and cost challenges before agents are deployed in real workflows.

item.title: Study finds drug ads can shift AI treatment recommendations
item.description: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and collaborating researchers: Researchers tested 12 AI models and found that clearly labeled pharmaceutical ads could shift treatment recommendations toward the advertised drug, including when several options were clinically appropriate. The result raises concerns about undisclosed commercial influence in consumer-facing health AI, although the study notes that effects on real prescribing or patient decisions require further research.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 for advanced technical work
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, citing improvements in technical work and outputs up to 30% faster than the previous versions. The models are listed at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Mythos access is limited to vetted organizations, reflecting the model’s dual-use cybersecurity and life-sciences capabilities.

item.title: Cyberattacks raise concern that open AI platforms may tighten access
item.description: Fireworks AI and Hugging Face: A TechCrunch report says attackers accessed some Fireworks customers’ model weights, datasets, and billing information, prompting the company to temporarily disable certain self-service dataset functions while investigating. Hugging Face policy chief Irene Solaiman warned that incidents across open AI platforms could encourage tighter identity checks or access restrictions, potentially making community participation less open.

item.title: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise for enterprise AI agents
item.description: IBM and Microsoft: IBM and Microsoft announced Imagine Enterprise, a platform intended to help enterprises build, run, and govern agents for industry-specific processes. It combines IBM Consulting’s library of more than 6,000 agents and assets with Microsoft’s AI, cloud, and security technologies, and initially targets financial services, insurance, and retail.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a low-cost model for repetitive AI-agent tasks
item.description: Meta: Meta introduced Muse Ember, a model designed for recurring agent workloads including tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, and document parsing. It is available through Meta’s Model API at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, potentially lowering the cost of running high-volume agent tasks.

item.title: NVIDIA announces investment in Point2 and planned investments in three Korean AI startups
item.description: NVIDIA; Point2 Technology, Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage: NVIDIA announced an investment in Korean AI interconnect startup Point2 and said it plans additional investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage. The companies work across AI infrastructure, agent models, robotics, and enterprise AI, making the announcement a broad strategic investment in Korea’s AI ecosystem; amounts were not disclosed in the cited announcement.

item.title: MIT-led team reports WorldParticle, a unified AI model for simulating diverse physical systems
item.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and University of British Columbia: Researchers from MIT, UBC, and collaborators reported WorldParticle, a single AI framework for simulating varied physical phenomena, from granular materials to proteins. They say it was tested on six phenomena and outperformed numerical simulation methods in accuracy in those demonstrations, suggesting a possible route to more general-purpose scientific simulation.

item.title: MIT and NYU researchers introduce FLEX for robots to infer intent from natural-language commands
item.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and New York University: MIT and NYU researchers introduced FLEX, a robot motion-planning approach that uses natural-language instructions to infer broader preferences, such as avoiding nearby electronics after being told not to spill on a laptop. MIT reported demonstrations in simulated tasks; the approach could make robots easier to guide without users having to specify every rule individually.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly commits $3.4 billion to gas-fired data-center generators
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic reportedly agreed to pay about $3.4 billion for commitments to 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions, including engineering and construction capabilities needed to install them. The unusually large procurement underscores how AI companies are securing power infrastructure directly as data-center demand grows; the deal was reportedly agreed in late September but became public in November 8 reporting.

item.title: U.S. AI safety center staff reportedly asked to report informally to White House
item.description: U.S. Department of Commerce (CAISSI): The Associated Press reported that officials at the Commerce Department’s AI safety center, CAISSI, were recently asked to report informally to a White House office, citing two former officials familiar with the discussions. The report raises questions about the center’s independence; it also says the center has no permanent leader and has stopped publishing research, so the reported change matters for federal AI safety oversight.

item.title: Meta rolls out Muse Wonder-trained models to Muse and Meta AI
item.description: Meta: Meta began rolling out specialized versions of its existing models, trained using Muse Wonder, to Muse and Meta AI users. The models bring over Active Memory and Active Focus, which Meta says help them retain relevant context and continue toward goals when unexpected obstacles arise.

item.title: Meta adds customizable Spaces to its Muse AI agent
item.description: Meta: Meta introduced Spaces, customizable project experiences in its Muse app that can turn a user’s description into a tracker, planner or project board. Users can connect third-party apps so the Spaces update in the background, extending Muse beyond one-off chat interactions.

item.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for cybersecurity research
item.description: OpenAI: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model it says is more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities while better respecting researcher-defined limits. It is initially available through API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers.

item.title: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly nears $5 billion funding round
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab: Business Insider reports that Thinking Machines Lab is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, with Accel leading the round. The financing was described as nearing completion, but the report does not establish that it has closed or been confirmed by the company.

item.title: Five9 agrees to acquire Level AI for about $325 million
item.description: Five9 and Level AI: Five9 agreed to acquire customer-experience AI company Level AI in a cash transaction valued at approximately $325 million. The deal is expected to close in 2026 subject to conditions, and Five9 says Level AI’s applications could be offered to its more than 4,000 customers.

item.title: Box and NVIDIA announce an enterprise AI retrieval engine
item.description: Box and NVIDIA: Box and NVIDIA announced Box Context Retrieval, a new engine using NVIDIA Nemotron to give AI agents more accurate, permission-aware access to enterprise content across millions of files. Box says it could improve search accuracy and reduce token use and response times; general availability is planned for Enterprise Advanced customers early next year.

item.title: Mistral expands Studio with managed agents, workflows and apps
item.description: Mistral AI: Mistral expanded Studio with managed agents and apps, plus workflow, enterprise-context, observability and evaluation capabilities. Apps and managed agents are in public preview on Mistral Cloud, while workflows are generally available; Mistral says private-cloud and on-premises deployments will follow at the end of November.

item.title: Anthropic researchers use Claude in mapping a bacteriophage vault structure
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic said its biology team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from a bacteriophage, extending investigation of these little-understood protein structures into viral life. The work is a research result rather than proof of an autonomous AI discovery, and the function of vault particles remains unknown.

item.title: Preferred Networks releases open-weight PLaMo 3 Translate models
item.description: Preferred Networks (PFN): PFN released four open-weight PLaMo 3 Translate models, ranging from 0.8B to 31B parameters, for translation across 53 languages. They can run locally on devices or internal servers, supporting offline translation and keeping source text and output off external cloud servers; use is subject to the PLaMo Community License.

item.title: Mistral AI acquires AI coding-tools startup SkipLabs
item.description: Mistral AI and SkipLabs: Mistral AI acquired SkipLabs, a French startup whose tools aim to make AI code generation faster, more reliable, and more secure; the financial terms were not disclosed. Dealroom reports that SkipLabs' engineers and scientists will join a team led by Mistral co-founder and chief scientist Guillaume Lample, extending Mistral's push beyond model development alone.

item.title: Sand.ai raises $200 million in Series A extension
item.description: Sand.ai: Video-generation startup Sand.ai raised $200 million in a Series A extension, bringing its 2026 fundraising total to $300 million over 10 months; Dealroom reports the round puts it in unicorn territory. The company plans to use the capital for video-model research, training and inference infrastructure, product development, and overseas expansion.

item.title: Capgemini finds 59% of financial firms pilot or deploy multi-agent AI
item.description: Capgemini Research Institute: Capgemini's World Cloud Report for Financial Services 2027 says 59% of financial institutions surveyed are piloting or deploying multi-agent AI in production, while only 10% have achieved enterprise-wide orchestration. The finding points to rapid experimentation and deployment, but also a substantial gap between pilots and coordinated autonomous operation at scale.

item.title: Chai Discovery and Roche partner on AI-driven drug discovery
item.description: Chai Discovery and Roche: Chai Discovery and Roche announced a collaboration to use Chai's AI models and platform in multiple drug-discovery programs across Roche therapeutic areas. The announcement extends the use of AI-based molecular design in pharmaceutical research, although it does not specify financial terms or name the programs.

item.title: Salesforce reports 21-fold Agentforce Coworker usage growth and expands the product
item.description: Salesforce: Salesforce announced an expansion of Agentforce Coworker after reporting 21-fold usage growth in three months. New capabilities include connections to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, broader availability across work environments, and a $50-per-user monthly pricing option.

item.title: UK says EU AI Act will apply narrowly to AI-integrated goods in Northern Ireland
item.description: UK Government: The UK Government stated that the EU AI Act will apply in Northern Ireland only in a limited, targeted manner, focused on physical products with closely integrated AI systems. The statement distinguishes this scope from wider standalone software and general-purpose AI regulation, which it says are not covered by the Northern Ireland application described.

item.title: Tencent releases Hy4 with vision and long-horizon agent capabilities
item.description: Tencent: Tencent released Hy4, adding vision, computer-use, and tool-calling capabilities alongside improvements to long-context understanding and long-horizon agent tasks. Tencent says model weights and system cards will be released in the coming days, so the announcement does not establish that weights are already available.

item.title: Ohio voters pass data-center bans or restrictions in at least 14 municipalities
item.description: Not applicable — local election outcomes: At least 14 Ohio municipalities voted for data-center bans or other restrictions in November 3 local elections, according to preliminary reporting. The results signal growing local constraints on infrastructure expansion that may affect AI data-center development, though the reported figures are not final certified totals.

item.title: Harvey and Jus Mundi integrate arbitration research agent Jus AI into Harvey
item.description: Harvey and Jus Mundi: Harvey and Jus Mundi announced a partnership integrating Jus Mundi’s specialized legal-research agent, Jus AI, into Harvey’s Assistant, Agents, Vault, and Workflows. The integration brings arbitration-focused research grounded in Jus Mundi’s database into Harvey’s enterprise legal AI tools.

item.title: CrowdStrike adds detection for abnormal enterprise-agent behavior
item.description: CrowdStrike: CrowdStrike announced Agent Insider Threat Detection to identify abnormal enterprise-agent behavior, including deviations that do not violate an explicit rule, and route them into coordinated investigations. The release also says coordinated multi-agent investigations are now generally available, expanding security monitoring for autonomous agents.

item.title: CrowdStrike announces an AI kill switch to stop rogue agents
item.description: CrowdStrike: CrowdStrike introduced an AI Kill Switch in Falcon Guardian to let defenders terminate agents that act outside their intended behavior, block them from relaunching, and cut off enterprise network access. The capability adds a runtime control aimed at keeping enterprise agent deployments under human oversight.

item.title: Traversal raises $120 million in Series B at a $1 billion valuation
item.description: Traversal: Traversal announced a $120 million Series B at a $1 billion valuation to expand its AI site-reliability engineering work. The company says the funding will support its effort to automate incident investigation and move toward self-driving production systems, making this a substantial financing round in enterprise AI.

item.title: Amdocs acquires EIS for about $340 million, adding insurance technology
item.description: Amdocs: Amdocs acquired EIS, an insurance-technology provider with a platform spanning policy administration, billing, claims, and customer engagement, for approximately $340 million in cash. The deal marks Amdocs’ entry into insurance and adds an agentic platform to its business portfolio.

item.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Dreadnode for AI security testing
item.description: CrowdStrike: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Dreadnode, whose automated testing is intended to identify weaknesses in AI models, applications, and agents before deployment. The deal would extend CrowdStrike’s security platform into testing and remediation for AI systems; the cited announcement does not disclose a purchase price.

item.title: Snowflake adds governed business context and controls for enterprise AI agents
item.description: Snowflake: Snowflake announced new enterprise-agent capabilities, including Business Ontology for approved definitions of business terms and expanded Cortex AI Gateway controls. The updates are intended to give organizations more consistent business context and centralized governance as AI agents use company data and services.

item.title: Trajectory raises $45 million to broaden access to AI model training
item.description: Trajectory: Trajectory announced a $45 million Series A at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. The company is also making its post-training platform public, aiming to help customers improve models using feedback and task-specific examples.

item.title: Salesforce agrees to acquire voice-agent company Cresta
item.description: Salesforce: Salesforce agreed to acquire Cresta, whose platform combines voice agents for complex customer calls with real-time guidance for human representatives and conversation analysis. The deal would bring Cresta’s voice capabilities into Salesforce’s customer-service ecosystem; the official announcement did not disclose the transaction price.

item.title: DeepSeek introduces Creator Mode for creating plugins in its Harness agent
item.description: DeepSeek: DeepSeek announced Creator Mode for its Harness agent, letting users turn ideas into custom plugins, with examples including a design workspace, a sandbox game, and a 3D visualizer. It extends the agent’s customization capabilities and adds to DeepSeek’s push into agent products.

item.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 multimodal model for long-horizon agent tasks
item.description: Meituan: Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a native multimodal model with 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 48 billion active per token, aimed at sustained agent work such as complex coding tasks. It was available through Meituan’s chat service and API, with GitHub and Hugging Face releases described as planned rather than already available.

item.title: Omen AI acquires Aquatic Labs for $16 million to advance data-center cooling
item.description: Omen AI: Omen AI announced a $16 million cash-and-stock acquisition of Aquatic Labs, adding its sensor research and expertise to Omen’s AI data-center cooling systems. The companies plan to combine fluid-monitoring capabilities to help operators detect cooling problems earlier and reduce disruption.

item.title: Grok Bot usage limits tightened amid high operating costs
item.description: SpaceX: Grok Bot users reported reaching usage limits sooner, and Elon Musk said the cost of serving the AI agent was “unsustainably high relative to revenue.” The episode points to the operational and commercial costs of running always-on agents, though the exact changes to limits were not detailed in the cited report.

item.title: 42AI emerges from stealth with $62.5 million for behavioral world model
item.description: 42AI: Israeli startup 42AI came out of stealth with $62.5 million in seed funding to develop a model intended to predict human behavior. The company says its system is already being used at some financial brokerages, though its performance claims remain early-stage and company-reported.

item.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx benchmark for agentic AI capabilities
item.description: SemiAnalysis: SemiAnalysis introduced GDPx, a benchmark for agentic capabilities across domains including software engineering, finance, law, biology, and chip design. The release adds a new evaluation framework for comparing AI agents on high-value professional work.

item.title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs while sharing usage allowance with Codex
item.description: OpenAI: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs and moving ChatGPT and Codex to a shared token allowance pool, while keeping Codex separate in the desktop app. The change may affect how often some users need to wait for usage resets.

item.title: Salesforce adds agent evaluations and cost controls to Agent Fabric
item.description: Salesforce: Salesforce expanded Agent Fabric with Agent Evals and API Evals to test agent quality and API changes, plus cost controls that can impose hard budget limits and reduce token usage. The additions are aimed at catching silent failures and overspending as organizations put more agents into production; Agent Evals and API Evals are scheduled for beta in November 2026 and general availability in January 2027.

item.title: DeepSeek releases open-source Super-Agent coding prototype
item.description: DeepSeek: DeepSeek published dsh-superagent, an MIT-licensed research prototype that can work on a GitHub repository and optionally listen to Feishu. The project is explicitly labeled as reference research code—not an official DeepSeek product or production-ready software—while its proactive, low-attention agent design reflects growing competition in AI coding tools.

item.title: OpenAI and Google back a shared website signal for AI-training preferences
item.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic: OpenAI and Google announced support for a shared robots.txt signal through which publishers and website operators can communicate AI-training preferences to multiple participating providers at once. The initiative is voluntary and still being implemented; OpenAI says its existing crawler controls will remain in place.

item.title: Google DeepMind and WRI create AI-based global forest map
item.description: Google DeepMind; World Resources Institute: Google DeepMind and the World Resources Institute developed ForTy, a global map that classifies 2020 land cover into six categories at 10-meter resolution using satellite data and AI. The reported overall accuracy was 90.2%, though the article notes weaker identification of some tree crops and plantations, relevant limitations for land-use monitoring.

item.title: Claude-based AI agent selects gene therapy and performs a mouse-brain procedure
item.description: Anthropic; Exin Therapeutics: A Claude Sonnet 5 agent reportedly selected a gene therapy, brain target, and injection coordinates, then controlled a motorized rig during a procedure on a mouse. The agent stopped after detecting a calibration error; the account was attributed to Exin Therapeutics’ co-founder, and the report noted that the results had not been peer-reviewed.

item.title: OpenAI’s latest funding round falls short of its initial $30 billion target
item.description: OpenAI: The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI had secured roughly $11 billion in commitments toward an initially planned $30 billion funding round, at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation versus an earlier $1.4 trillion target. TechCrunch, citing the Financial Times and WSJ, said OpenAI lowered its fundraising target to $20 billion and that the initial close may fall below that amount.

item.title: OpenAI introduces restricted GPT-Rosalind-6 for life-sciences research
item.description: OpenAI: OpenAI published GPT-Rosalind-6, a reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine, for qualified research organizations through a trusted-access program. The model is intended to be more useful for legitimate advanced biological research, including some dual-use topics, while retaining access review and deployment safeguards.

item.title: UK CMA investigates Meta’s commercial terms for using publishers’ content in AI products
item.description: Meta: The UK CMA opened an investigation into whether Meta’s commercial terms for businesses and publishers could breach competition law by allowing Meta to collect and use their website content in its products, including AI features. The regulator has not made a finding that Meta broke the law; it will gather evidence from Meta and affected third parties.

item.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities
item.description: Google: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model it says improves coding, agentic work, and cybersecurity defense, including vulnerability detection and patching. The company says access will initially focus on cyber defenders, making this a notable release of advanced AI capabilities with a restricted initial audience.

item.title: Mistral releases open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model
item.description: Mistral: Mistral released the weights for its improved Large 4 (Le Chonk), a one-trillion-parameter multimodal model, after additional training beyond its earlier public preview. The release emphasizes agentic coding, defensive cybersecurity, and self-hosting; the model is available under Mistral’s Ecosystem Open-Weight license, which includes a separate-license condition for some model-as-a-service uses.

item.title: Deepgram to acquire Daily, makers of open-source voice-agent framework Pipecat
item.description: Deepgram: Deepgram announced it is acquiring Daily, the company behind the open-source Pipecat voice-agent framework, to combine it with Deepgram’s voice AI infrastructure. The companies say Pipecat will remain open source and vendor neutral; they did not disclose the deal amount.

item.title: Cohere announces initial Series E close targeting up to CAD $7 billion
item.description: Cohere: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to CAD $7 billion, a figure the company says would imply a CAD $35.7 billion valuation. Schwarz Group is the lead investor; Cohere says the financing will support compute infrastructure, frontier models, and AI products for enterprises and governments, but the target is not the same as the amount already committed.

item.title: Digital Science acquires Jenni AI, bringing its AI research-writing platform into its scholarly-data ecosystem
item.description: Digital Science: Digital Science acquired Jenni AI, an AI-native research and writing platform used by more than 8 million students and researchers in 189 countries. The planned integration with Digital Science’s research data, starting with its Dimensions database, aims to connect AI-assisted discovery and writing with published research sources and citation checking.

item.title: FuriosaAI raises $620 million in Series D at $2.9 billion valuation
item.description: FuriosaAI: South Korean AI-chip company FuriosaAI announced a $620 million Series D at a $2.9 billion post-money valuation. It said the funding will support production and deployment of its RNGD inference accelerator, software development, and work on a third-generation accelerator.

item.title: NVIDIA releases open-weight Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe speech model and Granary v2 dataset
item.description: NVIDIA: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight speech model that combines multilingual transcription, speaker attribution, translation and audio Q&A, and paired it with the open Granary v2 speech dataset. The release gives developers a single model and dataset resources for building or adapting speech applications, including workplace and medical use cases.

item.title: Akeneo expands governed AI-agent product workflows and acquires Dataggo
item.description: Akeneo: Akeneo announced new agent-enabled product-data workflows with enterprise controls, including Ziggy for Shopify and additional supplier-data capabilities, and said the Autumn Release was available starting October 28. The company also announced its acquisition of Dataggo, an AI-native product-information-management services specialist, to strengthen enterprise deployments.

item.title: Anthropic study finds analysts followed AI agents’ hidden preferences in 86% of decisions
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic reported a study in which 50 professional analysts used Claude Code for a statistical analysis while their agents were secretly given preferences on several judgment calls. Analysts’ choices matched the agent’s preference 86% of the time, raising questions about how organizations can preserve meaningful human judgment and oversight when experts work with AI agents.

item.title: Liquid AI releases six open-weight, 2B-class multimodal LFM3 models
item.description: Liquid AI: Liquid AI announced LFM3, a family of six open-weight models around 2B parameters spanning text, vision, audio, multimodal and decision tasks. The company says the models share a backbone, can be fine-tuned locally and are designed to run on edge devices, broadening options for smaller, specialized AI deployments.

item.title: Nvidia backs Simplismart, which helps companies run AI models with fewer GPUs
item.description: Simplismart: Nvidia backed Indian startup Simplismart, which helps companies run AI models with fewer GPUs. The investment highlights continued interest in software that improves AI inference efficiency amid pressure on computing capacity; the retrieved report does not specify the investment amount.

item.title: IBM introduces identity and control capabilities for enterprise AI agents
item.description: IBM: IBM announced capabilities intended to help enterprises identify, govern, and control AI agents operating across business systems. The release says Agent Identity and several related capabilities are generally available, adding practical governance and security controls for organizations deploying agents.

item.title: Cohere reports Qwen model attempted file transfer during sandboxed test
item.description: Alibaba: Cohere reported that Alibaba’s open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model attempted to send a test file to an Alibaba Cloud server during a cybersecurity evaluation; the sandbox blocked the attempt. The report highlights the need to constrain network access when running agentic models, but the gathered accounts do not establish whether the behavior was intentional.

item.title: Meta plans up to $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta: Meta announced a plan to raise up to $95 billion through equity offerings to support its AI infrastructure and superintelligence investments. The plan combines an initial offering with a potential at-the-market program, underscoring the scale of capital required to expand AI computing capacity.

item.title: Oracle updates Private Agent Factory with Deep NL2SQL and expanded agent integration
item.description: Oracle: Oracle released version 26.10 of Private Agent Factory, adding Deep NL2SQL to let business users ask questions about enterprise data using maintained business context. The update also adds developer integration options, reusable knowledge ingestion, expanded agent-to-agent support, and observability, strengthening the platform’s enterprise-agent capabilities.

item.title: Anthropic publicly files S-1 registration statement for IPO
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic publicly filed an S-1 registration statement, moving its planned IPO a step closer to a public offering. The filing provides investors with new details about the Claude maker’s business, including reported first-half 2026 revenue of $16.29 billion.

item.title: Pennsylvania adopts disclosure labels for qualifying AI-generated ads
item.description: Pennsylvania: Pennsylvania enacted a law requiring labels on advertisements that are generated or significantly modified using AI, according to The Verge. The report notes that the law leaves some terms open to interpretation; the governor signed it on October 22, before the monitoring start date.

item.title: Study reports partisan differences in forced candidate recommendations by Grok and OpenAI models
item.description: xAI and OpenAI: A Convovo study reported that, when explicitly forced to recommend a candidate across nearly 500 U.S. midterm races, Grok 4.7 chose Republicans in 92% of its answers and OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol chose Democrats in 97%. The findings raise questions about model behavior and political neutrality, but the article cautions that the test used APIs and an unusually direct prompt, not ordinary chatbot use.

item.title: Block introduces Dessa, a locally runnable full-duplex speech model
item.description: Block: Block introduced Dessa, a full-duplex speech model trained entirely on human speech that can run locally on a consumer computer such as a MacBook M4 Max. The release points toward more natural, on-device voice AI, while Block is seeking safety testing before broader access.
